# Phase 1 Dose-Escalation Study of LY3484356 (a Novel FGFR Inhibitor) in Patients with Advanced Solid Tumors

## Background

LY3484356 is a selective, orally bioavailable inhibitor of fibroblast growth factor receptors 1-3 (FGFR1-3). Preclinical studies demonstrated potent antitumor activity in FGFR-altered tumor models. This Phase 1 first-in-human, open-label, dose-escalation study (NCT04781101) was designed to determine the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D), characterize safety and pharmacokinetics (PK), and assess preliminary antitumor activity.

## Methods

Adult patients with advanced solid tumors that had progressed on or were refractory to standard therapy were enrolled. The dose-escalation phase used a standard 3+3 design with five planned dose cohorts: 50 mg once daily (QD), 100 mg QD, 200 mg QD, 300 mg QD, and 400 mg QD. All doses were administered orally in continuous 28-day cycles. Dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) were assessed during Cycle 1. Intra-patient dose escalation was not permitted. PK sampling was performed on Days 1 and 15 of Cycle 1. Tumor assessments were performed every 8 weeks per RECIST v1.1. FGFR alteration status (amplification, mutation, or fusion) was assessed retrospectively from archival tissue.

## Results

Thirty-one patients were treated across the five dose cohorts: 50 mg (n=3), 100 mg (n=6), 200 mg (n=9), 300 mg (n=7), and 400 mg (n=6). All patients received LY3484356 as a single investigational agent on the dose-escalation study. No DLTs were observed at 50, 100, or 200 mg. Two DLTs (Grade 3 hyperphosphatemia) were observed at 300 mg; one DLT (Grade 3 stomatitis) occurred at 400 mg. The most common treatment-related adverse events were hyperphosphatemia (61%), dry mouth (48%), and fatigue (39%). PK was dose-proportional across all cohorts. The RP2D was established at 200 mg QD. Confirmed partial responses were observed in 5 patients (16%), all with FGFR alterations.

## Conclusion

LY3484356 demonstrated a manageable safety profile and preliminary antitumor activity in patients with advanced solid tumors. The five dose levels represent sequential safety cohorts within a single Phase 1 dose-escalation study of one investigational agent, not separate randomized treatment arms. The RP2D of 200 mg QD will be evaluated in subsequent Phase 2 expansion cohorts.
